label: Employment insurance on application: period that can be backdated
unit: days of service recoverable before the application
appliesTo: Foreign nationals on statuses where the Employment Insurance Act applies on application — E-1 to E-7, E-9, E-10, F-4, H-2 among them
why: The most consequential zero in Korean employment law for a foreign professional. Coverage on an application-based status begins the day after the application, so years already worked cannot be pulled back into the 180-day insured-days count. It converts what looks like a question to resolve when leaving into one that had to be settled on the first day of the job, and nothing on a payslip announces it.

history.source: Employment Insurance Act and its Enforcement Decree, application-based coverage for foreign nationals
history.note: Insured status generally arises from the day after the application is filed. An employee two years into a job who applies in month 21 does not thereby acquire 21 months of insured period. Where the Act applies in full — permanent residence and certain residence and marriage statuses — the question does not arise, because coverage never depended on an application.
